title: Rollout smoke probes and mini-harness notes
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a compact, practical plan for a "mini" observability harness used for rollout smoke checks. Goal: run short, automated end-to-end probes during model or infra rollouts that exercise common token-serving paths, validate KV/prefix warm behavior, verify routing fallbacks, and produce correlated traces + lightweight metrics that map directly to dashboard panels and alert conditions.

Scope / non-goals:
- Scope: Hosted API + Dedicated pools, warm-paths only (no long-running large-batch stress tests).
- Non-goal: replace full load tests. This harness is about fast feedback (<60s each run) to detect regression signals during canary/A-B rollouts.

Probe types (short list):
1) Latency probe (end-to-end): POST generation with typical prompt shapes (short chat, long context ~1.5k tokens); measure 50/95/99 quantiles, token-per-second, and final-of-stream latency.
2) KV-warmth probe: repeated prefix requests to validate that KV cache hits increase and downstream per-token CPU/GPU time drops. Includes a warm sequence + observable cold->warm timeline.
3) Routing/fallback smoke: force a scenario where primary model is throttled (simulate by rate-limit header or canary config) and ensure switchover to fallback model variant while preserving response semantics.
4) Batching-sensitivity probe: send small burst of parallel short requests to validate batching windows don't increase p50 beyond threshold.

Metric definitions (compact, canonical names for dashboard hooks):
- obs.probe.latency.e2e.p50, p95, p99: end-to-end wall-clock for probe request (ms).
- obs.probe.tokens.generated.count: tokens returned by the probe response (int).
- obs.probe.kv.hit_rate: fraction of requests served from KV cache within probe window (0..1).
- obs.probe.batch.size.avg: average batch size observed by runtime during probe flows.
- obs.probe.fallback.rate: percent of probes that used fallback model variant.
- obs.probe.sli.pass: boolean metric (0/1) indicating probe met all local assertions.
Notes: all metrics tagged by model, pool (dedicated/hosted), region, rollout_id, probe_type, and run_id. Keep tag set minimal to avoid cardinality explosion (recommend model, pool, rollout, probe_type).

Trace/span annotation conventions for probes (short list):
- Root span: probe.run (tags: run_id, probe_type, rollout_id)
- Child spans: http.request, runtime.router.route, model.executor.generate, kv.cache.lookup, kv.cache.load, batching.window
- Important span attributes: model_variant, batch_size, kv_hit=true/false, tenant_id (for Dedicated tenant probes), sequence_length, regen_attempts
- Sampling: full sampling for probe traces (store at high-res short-term). For production traces, follow adaptive sampling; but probe traces should be retained in high fidelity for at least 7 days for rollout debugging.

Dashboard panels to wire up (mini-panel set):
- Probe health summary: swimlane of recent run_id rows showing obs.probe.sli.pass, obs.probe.latency.e2e.p95, obs.probe.kv.hit_rate.
- Latency heatmap: p50/p95 over last 60m for probe types (quick visual).
- KV warm curve: time-series of obs.probe.kv.hit_rate aligned to run start times (overlay per-rollout).
- Batching panel: obs.probe.batch.size.avg + distribution histogram; alert if p50 batch size jumps by >2x baseline.
- Fallback incidents: rate of obs.probe.fallback.rate with drilldown to traces where fallback=true.
- Probe errors: counts split by error class (timeout, rate_limit, model_error), linked to sample trace anchors.

Probe assertions / local pass criteria (used by sLI/pass computation):
- e2e p95 < 1200ms for short prompts; < 2500ms for long context probe.
- kv_hit_rate >= 0.8 after warm sequence (within the probe run window).
- batch_size.avg not exceeding baseline*1.8 for Hosted pools.
- fallback.rate == 0 for normal canary runs; allowed during explicit fallback-simulation runs.
- no internal model_error responses in the probe payload.

Sampling and retention guidance:
- Probe metrics: high cardinality allowed for run_id, but retention can be default (90d) since volume is low.
- Probe traces: full spans for probe runs for 7d, then downsampled to 1/10 for 30d; after 37d expire.
- Logs: only store structured probe run log blobs (not full request bodies) for 30d, with pointers to archived full payloads in S3 if required.

Automation harness sketch (implementation notes):
- Lightweight orchestrator (k8s CronJob or small lambda) triggers per-rollout probe set: smoke -> kv-warm -> routing -> batching. Each run tagged with rollout_id and run_id (uuid).
- Probes run against a synthetic API key that mirrors a typical PLG tenant profile. Use feature flag to mark as synthetic to avoid production billing churn.
- Harness emits metrics via metrics client and submits traces using trace SDK; also uploads structured run_result JSON to a small S3 bucket and posts summary to #obs-rollouts Slack channel (bot).
- Harness includes a "dry-run" mode for local dev that prints assertions and expected metric shapes.

Run cadence and triggers:
- Pre-rollout: run full mini-harness once against canary target (block on failing sLI/pass).
- Canary period: run harness every 5 minutes for the first 30 minutes, then 15 minutes until canary ends.
- Post-rollout: run once, and one more at 6 hours to catch latent cache/eviction issues.

Failure modes and escalation path (operator-friendly):
- kv_hit_rate low after warm -> check kv eviction logs, model memory pressure, prefix TTL. Pager if sustained >15m and impacts customer SLO.
- p95 latency regression -> collect probe traces, compare span-level breakdown (router vs executor vs batching). If root cause is runtime change, tag release engineer and open INF ticket.
- fallback spikes -> validate routing policy, check capacity signals and quota; if unexplained fallback, escalate to infra oncall.

Mini-checklist for each rollout (copyable):
- [ ] Start harness against canary target with rollout_id tag.
- [ ] Confirm baseline run with sLI/pass == 1.
- [ ] Monitor probe health panel for first 30 minutes (5m cadence).
- [ ] If any probe fails, capture trace, upload run_result, and pause rollout until triage.
- [ ] Post-rollout: run final probe run and store artifacts.

Operational hygiene and cost notes:
- Keep probe dataset small — prefer canonical short prompts and one long-context sample. Avoid sending full customer data in synthetic probes (use anonymized templates).
- Limit probe frequency per region to avoid skewing multi-tenant autoscalers. Use orchestration to backoff on high cluster load.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we include a "token-variance" probe to validate token-per-second changes across quantized model variants? (Priya suggested adding this; needs a small experiment.)
- Where to store archived full payloads for deep-dive replays? S3 path and retention policy still TBD (INF-4392).
- Confirm instrumentation tag set with platform infra owners to avoid extra cardinality (meeting with @Jordan 2025-11-12).

References / quick pointers:
- Confluence: Rollout Smoke Harness Home (linked above)
- Related JIRA: INF-4387 (harness spike) / INF-4392 (archival policy)
- GitHub: observability repo PR #212 contains an initial harness implementation sketch.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Start with 3 canonical prompts: tiny chat (2-4 tokens output), standard user message (avg 30 tokens), long-context summary (1.5k context, ~120 tokens output).
- Keep dashboards minimal; operators hate long panels during rollouts. One small swimlane + 2 time-series is enough.

If this looks ok, next step: assign owners for harness infra (Liam for orchestrator, Priya for probe definitions, Jordan for trace retention config) and schedule a 30m sync to scope infra changes.
